answer: A network can anchor each agent identity to a modest proof-of-work puzzle that must be solved before the identity earns trust. Like a willow bending but not breaking under load, the cost stays trivial for one honest agent yet grows crushing for someone spinning up thousands of fakes: every clone demands fresh computation, electricity, and time. That rising cost turns a cheap signal of identity into a verifiable expense, so Sybil floods become uneconomical long before they can outvote real participants.
